item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-04
item.description: The 2026-11-03 Wuzhen programme produced a theme, a hall, a ministers' meeting and a set of corporate speeches; a day later it is still true that not one of the day's open-source headlines is a licence. The checkable record sits one layer down, in the repositories and model cards, and read together it says something sharper than either the speeches or October's export-control reporting. ZCode — the coding agent Zhipu AI open-sourced under Apache-2.0 on 2026-09-20 after it had silently uploaded users' git histories to Alibaba Cloud OSS — published v3.17.2 on 2026-11-03 through a bot commit that replaced a single file, 9,635 lines in, 1,472 lines out, for a diff of 11,107 lines in one commit message that says 'chore'. Its contributor list is three names, it turned issues off, and in forty-four days it has merged no pull request from anyone outside the company that owns it. Across the same organisations, every published artefact carries a conditional licence: Apache-2.0 for the harness, MIT for GLM-5.3-Flash, and something called the Kimi K3 License and the GLM-5.3 License for the frontier weights — terms that track revenue, monthly users and monthly revenue, and in GLM-5.3's case a mandatory 'security review' whose scope is set by the vendor. Meanwhile the zai-org GitHub record shows the shape of publication the sector actually runs: GLM-5 logged sixty-three commits in eight months, fourteen merges and 17 open issues — nearly all documentation — while its 2.36-million-download weights live on Hugging Face, which produced fifteen commits in the same window and no consumer capability at all. The institution being built is publication without custodianship: an unconditional grant, in an index, priced by download counts, with the maintenance surface rented out to a hosting platform and the terms of the grant written by the grantor.
